title: Designing with exceptions
idea: Good error handling makes every failure explicit: a method succeeds, or it signals a named failure the caller can see and act on.
points: Validate inputs first and throw before any state changes.
Throw unchecked exceptions for bugs and broken business rules.
Use checked exceptions only when the caller can really recover.
Translate low-level exceptions at a layer boundary, and keep the cause.

steps.caption: The service calls `store.read` inside a `try` block.
The disk fails. `read` throws a checked `IOException`, so its signature must declare it.
The service catches it and throws `ProfileUnavailableException`, passing the `IOException` as its cause.
`main` catches a domain exception. It never needs to know a disk was involved.
`getCause()` still holds the original error, so logs keep the full story.

code.title: Fail fast, name the failure
code.caption: One method, three outcomes: success, a business refusal, and a caller bug.

walk.text: A base domain exception, unchecked, with a stable `code()` callers can match on.
Each subclass names one failure and builds a useful message.
A bad argument is a caller bug: throw `IllegalArgumentException` at once.
Check the business rule next. The balance changes only after every check passes.
Catch the most specific types you can act on, in separate blocks.

code.title: Translate at the boundary
code.caption: A storage failure becomes a domain exception, and the original error rides along as its cause.

walk.text: `throws IOException` forces every caller to catch it or declare it.
The service catches it and rethrows a domain exception with the cause.
Pass `cause` to the `RuntimeException` constructor; `getCause()` returns it later.
The caller handles one domain type and can still read the root cause.

pitfalls: Never catch an exception and do nothing; log it, rethrow it or handle it.
Do not return `null` or `-1` for failure; throw or return `Optional`.
When you wrap an exception, pass the original as the cause.

quiz.q: Using the classes above, what does this print?
options: A stack trace from an uncaught exception
quiz.why: The guard `amount <= 0` runs first and throws `IllegalArgumentException`. It is not an `AccountException`, so the second `catch` block handles it.

takeaway: Fail fast, throw named exceptions, and keep the cause when translating.
